history.summary: NON-TEMPLE HERITAGE RECORD: KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED - Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava is the colossal ~30-ft-high rock-cut Shiva head (with a 10-ft embroidered headdress), the centrepiece of the open-air Unakoti Shaivite pilgrimage site, not a temple building. RELATED RECORD: the full Unakoti site is already documented as seq 1038 (id unakoti-rock-carvings) - this row names its central carving; recommend folding into seq 1038 or keeping as a sub-feature entry. The head sits in the stream bed flanked by two full-size female figures, one of them Durga standing on a lion. Unakoti ('one less than a crore') is an ASI-protected site on the UNESCO World Heritage tentative list (2022). Bas-relief sculptures are ascribed to the 7th-9th centuries CE (pre-Manikya period), patronised by the Deva Dynasty of Sribhumi in Samatata; the only inscription is an 11th-12th-century Bengali-script record of a pilgrim named Sri Jayadeva on a Chaturmukhalinga. Legend: Shiva, travelling to Kashi with one crore gods and goddesses, halted here overnight; when they failed to wake before sunrise he cursed them to become stone - hence 'one less than a crore' (local Kokborok name: Subrai Khung). Variant legend credits a devotee, Kallu Kumhar. First noted in 1914 by Captain Williams, detailed in the ASI annual report of 1921-22.

name: Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava
town: Unakoti (near Kailashahar; CSV town 'Unakoti' is the site name, ~8-9 km from Kailashahar town)
town_description: Unakoti is a forested hill site in Unakoti district, Tripura, about 8-9 km from the subdivision town of Kailashahar and roughly 125 km from Agartala. It is Tripura's prime tourist spot: an ASI-protected open-air Shaivite pilgrimage site of 7th-9th-century rock-cut carvings in a green, landscaped forest setting, on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list since 2022.

travel.airport: Nearest major airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala, about 125-140 km by road (verify); Kailashahar has a small non-scheduled airstrip (verify).
travel.railway: Kumarghat (about 27-30 km) or Dharmanagar (about 41 km) are the nearest railheads; hire a car onward (verify).
travel.road: About 8-9 km from Kailashahar; roughly 125 km from Agartala by road (verify). The site involves ~350 steps up and down - difficult for elderly visitors.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, the dry season; the Ashokastami Mela in March-April draws thousands.
visitor_information.opening_hours: No entry fee and no officially published hours reported; visit during daylight hours (verify). Carry water and food - no shops at the site.
